title: pkg/services conventions: interface segregation, store split, identity.Requester, typed errors, inline feature flags, mockery
answers: What conventions should I follow when writing a new service in pkg/services?
How is auth/user identity passed into service methods?
How are errors represented in services?
How are feature flags checked in service code?
How are mocks generated for service interfaces?
body:
- Interface segregation over one god-interface: `pkg/services/dashboards` root defines 5 separate interfaces (DashboardService, DashboardAccessService, PermissionsRegistrationService, PluginService, DashboardProvisioningService) all satisfied by one `DashboardServiceImpl` struct (see wire.Bind usage above).
- Store/service split: e.g. `pkg/services/star/starimpl/store.go` defines an unexported `store` interface, `star.go` holds business logic, `xorm_store.go` is the SQL impl — service code talks only to `store`, never the DB directly.
- Auth via `identity.Requester`, not raw user IDs: `pkg/services/dashboards/service/dashboard_service.go:104 HasDashboardAccess(ctx, user identity.Requester, ...)` using `claims.TypeUser`/`claims.TypeServiceAccount` from authlib/types.
- Errors are typed structs carrying HTTP status, not plain `errors.New`: `pkg/services/dashboards/errors.go` defines `ErrDashboardNotFound = dashboardaccess.DashboardErr{Reason: ..., StatusCode: 404, ...}`.
- Feature flags are checked inline via a held `features featuremgmt.FeatureToggles` field and `dr.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagX)` calls scattered through business logic (e.g. `dashboard_service.go:1273`) — there is no separate gating layer/middleware.
- Mocks are generated with `//go:generate mockery` directives placed directly above the interface they mock (e.g. `dashboards.go:19`), producing an in-package `FakeDashboardService`; ~39 such directives exist under pkg/services.
applies: General conventions across pkg/services domains; individual small services (e.g. star) may skip some (e.g. no feature-flag checks) but the store/service split and mockery pattern are broadly consistent.
